(a) All intra-university candidates seeking transfer to the Mechatronics Engineering Department must have a minimum CGPA of 3.6. (b) All inter-university candidates seeking transfer to the Mechatronics Engineering Department of the Federal University of Technology, Minna must: (i) be studying Mechatronics, Mechanical, Telecommunication, Computer, Electrical or Electronic Engineering in their current university; (ii) have passed all courses registered in their current university before seeking the transfer; (iii) have a minimum CGPA of 3.6 out of 5.00, or 3.00 on a scale of 4.00; and (iv) transfer cases can only be entertained up to, and not beyond, 200 Level. (c) In all cases, admission is purely based on available vacancies and the number of candidates applying for admission.

sections.title: Heads of Department and Administration
sections.text:
Previous and current Heads of the Department of Mechatronics Engineering: Professor M. J. E. Salami, 2014–2015; Professor A. M. Aibinu, 2015–2021; Professor J. G. Kolo, 2021 till date.

The current Head of Department is Engr. Prof. Jonathan Gana Kolo (B.Eng 1994, M.Sc. 2002, PhD 2013, COREN Registered). The departmental administrative staff includes Mr. Konyeha Silvester, Personal Secretary II (HND Secretarial Studies, 2006). The department's organogram runs from the Head of Department through committee and departmental officers to the academic, technical and administrative staff, with level advisers overseeing students.

sections.title: Staff Contributions to Engineering and Industry
sections.text: Members of staff contribute to the engineering profession within and outside the University. They actively participate in the activities of professional associations such as the Nigerian Society of Engineers (NSE) and the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN). Staff also offer consultancy services in specialized areas including robotics, avionics, computer maintenance and networking, artificial intelligence, military equipment production and automation. The department is presently working with the Nigerian Air Force, the Nigerian Army and the Nigeria Space Defense Institute on some military-related projects. The department has participated in various local and international exhibitions and won Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) and Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFUND) awards in 2013, 2014 and 2015. In addition, the department hosted the maiden edition of the Nigeria Robotics Championship (NIROC) in 2013.

sections.title: University Library and e-Library
sections.text: The University has a large collection of required, current and quality books, journal papers and relevant literature for students in the University Library and in the Faculty Library. The department is also equipped with a state-of-the-art electronic library accessible to both students and staff; the departmental e-Library is accessible at the SICT Library, and additional resources can be obtained from the university e-Library. The departmental website can be accessed at https://futminna.edu.ng/seet/mce/.

sections.title: Departmental Activities
sections.text: Departmental activities include: (a) the Orientation Programme; (b) the sessional HOD briefing; (c) the Robotics, Programmers and Embedded Systems Club; (d) the Mentor and Mentee Project; (e) the Nigeria Robotics Championship (NIROC); (f) departmental tutorials; and (g) the Departmental Students' Association.

sections.title: Laboratory Facilities
sections.text: The department and the faculty are equipped with a number of laboratories, including: Mechatronics Laboratory 1; Mechatronics Laboratory 2; Mechatronics Lab 1 and Lab 2 in the Central Teaching Lab; two further Central Teaching Labs; the Intermediate, Transmission Line, Fiber Optic, Microwave and Networking Laboratory; the Electronics Laboratory; the Control and Instrumentation Laboratory; the Power and Machine Laboratory; the Robotics and Automation Workshop; the Electrical Power Laboratory; the Embedded System Laboratory; the Telecommunication Laboratories; the AutoCAD Laboratory; the CAD/CAM Laboratory; and the 3D Printing and PCB Laboratory.

sections.title: Appraisal of Facilities, Teaching Aids and Safety
sections.text:
Generally, the quantity and quality of facilities are adequate, though the Department is growing; considerable effort is being made by the University management for rapid expansion of facilities to eliminate present inadequacies.

Teaching aids: a public address system and multimedia projectors are provided by the School as teaching aids in the Lecture Theatre. The department also provides multimedia projectors and laptops for teaching and administrative purposes.

Safety in laboratories: in the course of laboratory and workshop practice, safety precautions such as a clean working space, wearing protective gear and avoiding electric shock are seriously emphasized. First aid boxes are available in case of emergency in all laboratories and workshops. Fire prevention measures, like the avoidance of inflammable materials in the laboratories, are observed; fire-fighting equipment such as CO2 and foam extinguishers and sand buckets are provided in the laboratory, and the University has a fire van strategically stationed.
